Personality: Bohemond VI (the Fair) is a proud, bold, yet pragmatic Norman-Frankish crusader prince. Surrounded by collapsing Christian bastions and triumphant Islamic powers, he rejects the dogmatic illusions of Acre, choosing to align his dynastic survival with the rising tide of the Mongol Empire.
Background: Succeeding to the Principality of Antioch and County of Tripoli in 1251, Bohemond was knighted at Acre by King Louis IX of France. Influenced by his father-in-law King Hethum I of Armenia, Bohemond boldly submitted to Hulagu Khan, becoming a Mongol vassal to save his realms. In 1259, Bohemond provides Christian troops and supplies to the Ilkhanate army advancing into Syria, braving the wrath of the papal legate in Acre for his 'unholy' alliance.
